visibility.description: partial when the role lacks pg_read_all_stats (pg_monitor): the replication views hide their columns; an empty or null view is then not proof of anything

database.description: The database the connection is in

currentLsn.description: pg_current_wal_lsn(), read once: every distance in this output is from this position

replicas.description: pg_stat_replication: one entry per connected walsender, standbys and also pg_basebackup, pg_receivewal and logical-replication walsenders; an empty list is a primary with none connected. Cut to maxItems in the query

applicationName.description: The standby's application_name (its cluster_name or walreceiver)

clientAddr.description: Address the standby connected from; null for a local socket (null where pg_stat_replication hides it from this role: visibility partial)

state.description: startup, catchup, streaming, backup or stopping (null where pg_stat_replication hides it from this role: visibility partial)

syncState.description: async, potential, sync or quorum (null where pg_stat_replication hides it from this role: visibility partial)

writeLagMs.description: Time from flushing local WAL until the standby wrote it; null when no recent measurement (an idle standby is not zero)

flushLagMs.description: Same until the standby flushed it

replayLagMs.description: Same until the standby replayed it

sentLsnBytes.description: pg_current_wal_lsn() minus sent_lsn, bytes not yet sent

writeLsnBytes.description: pg_current_wal_lsn() minus write_lsn, bytes not yet written by the standby

replayLsnBytes.description: pg_current_wal_lsn() minus replay_lsn, bytes the standby has not replayed

total.description: Entries found before the maxItems cap

omitted.description: Entries left out of items by maxItems

truncated.description: true when items was cut at maxItems

slots.description: pg_replication_slots; an empty list is a primary with no slot. Cut to maxItems in the query

active.description: true while a walsender or a client uses the slot

walStatus.description: reserved, extended, unreserved or lost; null when the slot has no restart_lsn

retainedWalBytes.description: pg_current_wal_lsn() minus restart_lsn: for a live slot, the WAL it keeps on disk; for a lost slot (walStatus lost) only a distance, WAL already removed is not on disk; null without a restart_lsn

safeWalSize.description: Bytes of WAL that can still be written before the slot is at risk of losing WAL (max_slot_wal_keep_size); null when unlimited and for a lost slot

total.description: Entries found before the maxItems cap

omitted.description: Entries left out of items by maxItems

truncated.description: true when items was cut at maxItems

receiver.description: pg_stat_wal_receiver; null when this standby has no WAL receiver running (archive recovery, or cut off from the sender)

status.description: streaming, starting, waiting, stopping...; null when hidden (visibility partial)

senderHost.description: Host of the primary the receiver is connected to

slotName.description: Slot the receiver uses, if any

lastMsgReceiptAgeMs.description: Milliseconds since the receiver last got a message from the sender (now minus last_msg_receipt_time); an idle primary still sends keepalives, so a streaming receiver keeps this small (below wal_receiver_timeout). Null when hidden (visibility partial)

latestEndLsn.description: latest_end_lsn: the last WAL position reported by the sender; null when hidden (visibility partial)

receiveLsn.description: pg_last_wal_receive_lsn(): the last WAL position received and flushed. It keeps its last value after the receiver exits, so it does not show the standby is still connected (see receiver and lastMsgReceiptAgeMs); null when WAL was never received

receivedNotReplayedBytes.description: Received minus replayed WAL, in bytes

receiveEqualsReplay.description: true when everything received has been replayed; with true, replayDelayMs measures how long ago the primary last committed, not a backlog, but only while receiver.status is streaming and receiver.lastMsgReceiptAgeMs is recent. With no receiver or a stale message the standby is cut off, whatever this says

replayDelayMs.description: clock_timestamp() minus pg_last_xact_replay_timestamp(), in milliseconds; null until a transaction has been replayed

replayPauseState.description: pg_get_wal_replay_pause_state(): not paused, pause requested or paused; null before PostgreSQL 14
